statement: The roots of $x^{2}+px+q=0$ are $\\alpha$ and $\\beta$. (i) Find, in terms of $p$ and $q$, the quadratic equation whose roots are $\\alpha^{2}$ and $\\beta^{2}$. (ii) Hence, when $p=-3$ and $q=2$, write down the new equation explicitly and its roots.
solution: By Vieta, $\\alpha+\\beta=-p$ and $\\alpha\\beta=q$. Then $\\alpha^{2}+\\beta^{2}=(\\alpha+\\beta)^{2}-2\\alpha\\beta=p^{2}-2q$ and $\\alpha^{2}\\beta^{2}=q^{2}$. So the required equation is $x^{2}-(p^{2}-2q)x+q^{2}=0$. With $p=-3,q=2$: $x^{2}-(9-4)x+4=x^{2}-5x+4=0=(x-1)(x-4)$, roots $1,4$ (which are indeed $(-1)^{2}$ and $(-2)^{2}$).
hints: Use $\\alpha+\\beta$ and $\\alpha\\beta$ to build the new sum and product.
Substitute the given numbers at the end.
